## P3 - Failed `Check SR-SIM License` suppresses all diagnostic evidence and reports unmeasured values

**Location:** [tests/srsim.robot:30-41](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L30-L41)

**Problem:** `Check SR-SIM License` sets the log level to `NONE` for the entire 45-second retry window. Because `Run` logs command stdout at `INFO` level, all collected evidence &#40;`${runtime} ps -aq ...`, `${runtime} logs ... \| grep ...`, the boot-log `grep -R`, and every excerpt&#41; is suppressed. On failure the test is failed with only the static message `SR-SIM boot log has no license result`, and the not-found branch additionally prints `License renewal required: yes` for a measurement that never happened.

**Trigger:** Any failed license check&#58; the license line is not flushed within 45 seconds on a slow runner, the `TiMOS` log wording changes, or the runtime is unreachable. This surfaces in the [`srsim-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/.github/workflows/srsim-tests.yml#L1-L1) CI artifacts.

**Impact:** Maintainers cannot distinguish a boot-timing flake from a pattern mismatch or a runtime failure without re-running the suite manually, which undermines the diagnosability purpose of the new check.

**Suggested correction:** In the failure branch, restore the log level &#40;or log at a level that passes the filter&#41;, call `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt` once more and log the excerpt and resolved container names before `Fail`. Drop the synthesized `License renewal required: yes` line on the not-found path; `License expiration: not found` alone is honest.


## P4 - `docker ps -aq` with `--format '{{.Names}}'` returns container IDs, not names

**Location:** [tests/srsim.robot:60-62](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L60-L62)

**Problem:** In the Docker CLI, `-q` takes precedence over `--format`, so `${names}` contains container IDs rather than the names the template requests. The keyword only works because `docker logs` also accepts IDs. Podman resolves the `--format`/`-q` combination differently, so the two runtimes would return different values from the same command. Elsewhere in the repo the same pattern is written correctly, for example in [`tests/13-srsim/09-srsim-pause-container.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/13-srsim/09-srsim-pause-container.robot#L1-L1) &#40;`docker ps -a --filter ... --format '{{.Names}}'` without `-q`&#41;.

**Trigger:** Every execution of `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt` under Docker, which is the only runtime that reaches these suites today.

**Impact:** No functional failure today, but the format string is dead code that misleads readers into thinking container names are collected, and it creates a latent runtime divergence if a future Podman-enabled suite reuses the keyword.

**Suggested correction:** Drop `-q` and keep `--format '{{.Names}}'`, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the test suite, or drop `--format` and treat the values as IDs explicitly.


## P4 - License regex and grep patterns are duplicated across three keywords in [`tests/srsim.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L1-L1)

**Location:** [tests/srsim.robot:48-85](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L48-L85)

**Problem:** The `TiMOS` license-load regex appears verbatim in both `Boot Log Contains License Result` &#40;line 50&#41; and `Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log` &#40;line 80&#41;, and the four-alternative grep pattern appears verbatim in both the per-container command &#40;line 66&#41; and the boot-log command &#40;line 70&#41;. The paired `Log To Console` plus `Log` calls &#40;four lines for two messages, repeated twice&#41; and the second `Set Log Level NONE`/`INFO` pair in `Report` extend the same duplication.

**Trigger:** Any future adjustment, such as `TiMOS` changing the license-load wording, must be applied in multiple places; missing one makes the waiting keyword succeed while the report keyword silently misclassifies the license.

**Impact:** Divergence risk in exactly the logic this PR is meant to centralize.

**Suggested correction:** Define the license regex and grep pattern once as suite-level variables in the `*** Variables ***` section of [`tests/srsim.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L1-L1), reuse them from all call sites, and collapse the duplicated reporting lines.


## Coverage

- Source-only review; no tests were executed and no `TiMOS` boot-log output was observed, so the exact log line formats and the timing of the license-load line could not be verified against real data.
- The 45-second total budget in `Check SR-SIM License` is intentional but unvalidated; if `TiMOS` prints the license line later on slow runners, all suites using `Deploy SR-SIM Lab` could flake. Not reported as a finding for lack of evidence.
- The report treats any captured expiration date as renewal required &#40;`len($dates) > 0`&#41;. Per the keyword documentation &#40;&#39;Expiration is printed only when the log contains it&#39;&#41; this appears intentional; if `TiMOS` printed expiry on every boot, all license-gated suites would fail. Noted as a risk, not a defect.
- Stale `bootlog.txt` files from a previous un-cleaned lab run could theoretically satisfy the check with old content; every exercising suite destroys with `--cleanup`, so the exposure is limited and not reported as a finding.
- Verified&#58; component and netns-holder containers inherit the `clab-node-kind=nokia_srsim` label &#40;deep copy of `n.Cfg` in [`nodes/sros/sros.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1-L1) with labels set by [`core/config.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/core/config.go#L1-L1)&#41;, all referenced topologies declare `kind: nokia_srsim`, all callers run in test scope so the `Set Test Variable` handoff is safe, and both exercising suites are Docker-only &#40;[`12-srsim-multi-mgmt.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/15-mgmt/12-srsim-multi-mgmt.robot#L1-L1) skips on non-Docker runtimes; the `13-srsim` CI shard uses the default docker runtime&#41;.
- No documentation or schema impact&#58; the change is confined to test code with no user-visible CLI or topology behavior.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

If uncertain, ask.\n- If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.\n- If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.\n- If something is unclear, stop. Surgical Changes\n\n**Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**\n\nWhen editing existing code:\n\n- Don't \"improve\" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.\n- Don't refactor things that aren't broken.\n- Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.\n- If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.\n\nWhen your changes create orphans:\n\n- Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.\n- Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.\n\nThe test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.\n\n## 4. 1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

1: *** Settings ***
2: Library             OperatingSystem
3: Resource            ../common.robot
4: Resource            ../ssh.robot
5: 
6: Suite Setup         Run Keyword    Cleanup
7: Suite Teardown      Run Keyword    Cleanup
8: 
9: 
10: *** Variables ***
11: ${lab-name}                 srsim-apply
12: ${topo}                     11-srsim-apply.clab.yml
13: ${no-links-vars}            11-srsim-apply.vars.no-links.yml
14: ${linked-vars}              11-srsim-apply.vars.linked.yml
15: ${linked-with-node-vars}    11-srsim-apply.vars.linked-with-node.yml
16: ${runtime}                  docker
17: ${recovery-timeout}         3 minutes
18: ${boot-timeout}             5 minutes
19: ${retry-interval}           10 seconds
20: 
21: 
22: *** Test Cases ***
23: Apply initial lab without links has no client connectivity
24:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    ${no-links-vars}
25:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
26:     # a fresh deployment prints the container inspect table and no reconciliation summary
27:     Should Contain    ${output}    clab-${lab-name}-client
28:     Should Not Contain    ${output}    Apply summary
29:     # no links yet: client cannot reach either SR-SIM node
30:     Client Cannot Ping    10.0.1.2
31:     Client Cannot Ping    10.0.2.2
32: 
33: Apply adds links to SR-SIM nodes and connectivity succeeds
34:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    ${linked-vars}
35:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
36:     Should Contain    ${output}    added links
37:     Configure Client Interface    eth1    10.0.1.1/24
38:     Configure Client Interface    eth2    10.0.2.1/24
39:     # standalone SR-SIM
40:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${recovery-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    Client Can Ping    10.0.1.2
41:     # distributed SR-SIM
42:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${recovery-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    Client Can Ping    10.0.2.2
43: 
44: Stopping the SR-SIM nodes breaks connectivity
45:     Stop Node    R1
46:     Stop Node    R2
47:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
48:     ...    docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' clab-${lab-name}-R1 clab-${lab-name}-R2-a clab-${lab-name}-R2-1
49:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
50:     Should Be Equal As Strings    ${output}    false\nfalse\nfalse
51:     Client Cannot Ping    10.0.1.2
52:     Client Cannot Ping    10.0.2.2
53: 
54: Apply restarts the stopped SR-SIM nodes and unparks their links
55:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    ${linked-vars}
56:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
57:     Should Contain    ${output}    started nodes
58:     Should Contain    ${output}    Restored link
59:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${recovery-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    Client Can Ping    10.0.1.2
60:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${recovery-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    Client Can Ping    10.0.2.2
61: 
62: Apply adds a components-based SR-SIM node that boots with its cards up
63:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    ${linked-with-node-vars}
64:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
65:     Should Contain    ${output}    added nodes
66:     Should Contain    ${output}    R3
67:     # node boots and is reachable over SSH
68:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${boot-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    SR-SIM SSH Reachable    R3
69:     # CPM, IOM and configured MDA all report up
70:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${boot-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    SR-SIM Cards Up    R3
71: 
72: Apply recreates a running distributed node and restores its links
73:     ${rc}    ${cpm} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
74:     ...    docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' clab-${lab-name}-R2-a
75:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
76:     ${rc}    ${peer} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
77:     ...    docker exec clab-${lab-name}-client cat /sys/class/net/eth2/ifindex
78:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
79:     Set Suite Variable    ${client-peer-index}    ${peer}
80:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    11-srsim-apply.vars.recreate.yml
81:     Log    ${output}
82:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
83:     Should Contain    ${output}    Restored link
84:     ${rc}    ${replacement} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
85:     ...    docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' clab-${lab-name}-R2-a
86:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
87:     Should Not Be Equal As Strings    ${cpm}    ${replacement}
88:     Verify Distributed Links Recovered
89: 
90: Apply removes a distributed node
91:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
92:     ...    docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' clab-${lab-name}-R3-a clab-${lab-name}-R3-1
93:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
94:     Should Be Equal As Strings    ${output}    true\ntrue
95:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Apply    ${linked-vars}
96:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
97:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
98:     ...    docker ps -a --filter name=clab-${lab-name}-R3 --format '{{.Names}}'
99:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
100:     Should Be Empty    ${output}
101: 
102: *** Keywords ***
103: Verify Distributed Links Recovered
104:     Wait Until Keyword Succeeds    ${recovery-timeout}    ${retry-interval}    Client Can Ping    10.0.2.2
105:     ${rc}    ${peer} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
106:     ...    docker exec clab-${lab-name}-client cat /sys/class/net/eth2/ifindex
107:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
108:     Should Be Equal As Strings    ${peer}    ${client-peer-index}
109: 
110: Apply
111:     [Arguments]    ${vars_file}
112:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
113:     ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} apply -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${vars_file} 2>&1
114:     Log    ${output}
115:     RETURN    ${rc}    ${output}
116: 
117: Stop Node
118:     [Arguments]    ${node}
119:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
120:     ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} stop -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} -n ${node} 2>&1
121:     Log    ${output}
122:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
123: 
124: Configure Client Interface
125:     [Arguments]    ${interface}    ${address}
126:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
127:     ...    ${runtime} exec clab-${lab-name}-client ip link set dev ${interface} up
128:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0    ${output}
129:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
130:     ...    ${runtime} exec clab-${lab-name}-client ip addr add ${address} dev ${interface}
131:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0    ${output}
132: 
133: Client Can Ping
134:     [Arguments]    ${destination}
135:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
136:     ...    ${runtime} exec clab-${lab-name}-client ping -c2 -W2 ${destination}
137:     Log    ${output}
138:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
139:     Should Match Regexp    ${output}    2 packets transmitted, 2 (packets )?received, 0% packet loss
140: 
141: Client Cannot Ping
142:     [Arguments]    ${destination}
143:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
144:     ...    ${runtime} exec clab-${lab-name}-client ping -c2 -W2 ${destination}
145:     Log    ${output}
146:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    1
147:     Should Match Regexp    ${output}    2 packets transmitted, 0 (packets )?received,.*100% packet loss
148: 
149: SR-SIM SSH Reachable
150:     [Arguments]    ${node}
151:     Login via SSH with username and password
152:     ...    address=clab-${lab-name}-${node}
153:     ...    username=admin
154:     ...    password=NokiaSros1!
155:     ...    try_for=20
156:     ...    conn_timeout=3
157:     SSHLibrary.Close All Connections
158: 
159: SR-SIM Cards Up
160:     [Arguments]    ${node}
161:     # 'show card state' for an sr-1-24d lists slot 1 (IOM), 1/1 (MDA) and A (CPM),
162:     # each with "<admin> <oper>" states. Assert all three are operationally up.
163:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
164:     ...    echo "show card state" | sshpass -p 'NokiaSros1!' ssh -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null admin@clab-${lab-name}-${node}
165:     Log    ${output}
166:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
167:     # CPM (slot A): "A   cpm-1x   up   up"
168:     Should Match Regexp    ${output}    (?m)^A\\s+\\S+\\s+up\\s+up
169:     # IOM (slot 1): "1   i24-...   up   up"
170:     Should Match Regexp    ${output}    (?m)^1\\s+\\S+\\s+up\\s+up
171:     # MDA (slot 1/1) must finish booting too.
172:     Should Match Regexp    ${output}    (?m)^1/1\\s+\\S+\\s+up\\s+up
173: 
174: Cleanup
175:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
176:     ...    ${CLAB_BIN} --runtime ${runtime} destroy -t ${CURDIR}/${topo} --vars ${CURDIR}/${linked-with-node-vars} --cleanup
177:     Log    ${output}
178:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
179:     ${rc}    ${output} =    Run And Return Rc And Output
180:     ...    ${runtime} ps -a --filter label=containerlab=${lab-name} --format '{{.Names}}'
181:     Should Be Equal As Integers    ${rc}    0
182:     Should Be Empty    ${output}

(End of file - total 182 lines)
</content>

57:     steps:

1: name: test-srsim
2: 
3: "on":
4:   issue_comment:
5:     types: [created]
6: 
7: jobs:
8:   authorize:
9:     if: >-
10:       github.event.issue.pull_request &&
11:       contains(github.event.comment.body, '/test srsim')
12:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
13:     permissions:
14:       contents: read
15:       issues: write
16:       pull-requests: read
17:     outputs:
18:       authorized: ${{ steps.authorize.outputs.authorized }}
19:       head_sha: ${{ steps.authorize.outputs.head_sha }}
20:       test_ref: ${{ steps.authorize.outputs.test_ref }}
21:     steps:
22:       - name: Verify command and permissions
23:         id: authorize
24:         uses: actions/github-script@v9
25:         with:
26:           script: |
27:             const command = context.payload.comment.body.trim();
28:             if (command !== '/test srsim') {
29:               core.setOutput('authorized', 'false');
30:               return;
31:             }
32: 
33:             let authorized = false;
34:             try {
35:               const { data } = await github.rest.repos.getCollaboratorPermissionLevel({
36:                 owner: context.repo.owner,
37:                 repo: context.repo.repo,
38:                 username: context.payload.comment.user.login,
39:               });
40:               authorized =
41:                 ['admin', 'maintain'].includes(data.role_name) ||
42:                 data.permissions?.admin === true ||
43:                 data.permissions?.maintain === true;
44:             } catch (error) {
45:               if (error.status !== 404) throw error;
46:             }
47: 
48:             core.setOutput('authorized', String(authorized));
49: 
50:             if (!authorized) {
51:               await github.rest.issues.createComment({
52:                 owner: context.repo.owner,
53:                 repo: context.repo.repo,
54:                 issue_number: context.issue.number,
55:                 body: 'Only repository maintainers can run `/test srsim`.',
56:               });
57:               return;
58:             }
59: 
60:             const { data: pullRequest } = await github.rest.pulls.get({
61:               owner: context.repo.owner,
62:               repo: context.repo.repo,
63:               pull_number: context.issue.number,
64:             });
65:             core.setOutput('head_sha', pullRequest.head.sha);
66:             core.setOutput('test_ref', pullRequest.merge_commit_sha || pullRequest.head.sha);
67: 
68:   create-check:
69:     needs: authorize
70:     if: needs.authorize.outputs.authorized == 'true'
71:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
72:     permissions:
73:       checks: write
74:     outputs:
75:       check_run_id: ${{ steps.create.outputs.check_run_id }}
76:     steps:
77:       - name: Create PR check
78:         id: create
79:         uses: actions/github-script@v9
80:         env:
81:           HEAD_SHA: ${{ needs.authorize.outputs.head_sha }}
82:         with:
83:           script: |
84:             const { data: checkRun } = await github.rest.checks.create({
85:               owner: context.repo.owner,
86:               repo: context.repo.repo,
87:               name: 'srsim-tests (manual)',
88:               head_sha: process.env.HEAD_SHA,
89:               status: 'in_progress',
90:               details_url: `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`,
91:               external_id: String(context.runId),
92:               output: {
93:                 title: 'srsim tests are running',
94:                 summary: 'Triggered by `/test srsim`.',
95:               },
96:             });
97:             core.setOutput('check_run_id', String(checkRun.id));
98: 
99:   load-vars:
100:     needs: authorize
101:     if: needs.authorize.outputs.authorized == 'true'
102:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
103:     outputs:
104:       go_ver: ${{ steps.vars.outputs.go_ver }}
105:       py_ver: ${{ steps.vars.outputs.py_ver }}
106:       uv_ver: ${{ steps.vars.outputs.uv_ver }}
107:     steps:
108:       - uses: actions/checkout@v7
109:         with:
110:           ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
111:           sparse-checkout: .github/vars.env
112:           sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
113:           persist-credentials: false
114:       - id: vars
115:         run: |
116:           source .github/vars.env
117:           echo "go_ver=$GO_VER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
118:           echo "py_ver=$PY_VER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
119:           echo "uv_ver=$UV_VER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
120: 
121:   build-containerlab:
122:     needs:
123:       - authorize
124:       - create-check
125:       - load-vars
126:     if: needs.authorize.outputs.authorized == 'true'
127:     strategy:
128:       matrix:
129:         include:
130:           - runner: ubuntu-24.04
131:             arch: amd64
132:           - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
133:             arch: arm64
134:     uses: ./.github/workflows/build-containerlab.yml
135:     permissions:
136:       contents: read
137:       actions: read
138:       packages: read
139:     with:
140:       go_ver: ${{ needs.load-vars.outputs.go_ver }}
141:       runner: ${{ matrix.runner }}
142:       arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
143:       ref: ${{ needs.authorize.outputs.test_ref }}
144: 
145:   srsim-tests:
146:     needs:
147:       - authorize
148:       - create-check
149:       - load-vars
150:       - build-containerlab
151:     if: needs.authorize.outputs.authorized == 'true'
152:     uses: ./.github/workflows/srsim-tests.yml
153:     permissions:
154:       contents: read
155:       actions: read
156:       packages: read
157:     secrets:
158:       SRSIM_LICENSE: ${{ secrets.SRSIM_LICENSE }}
159:     with:
160:       py_ver: ${{ needs.load-vars.outputs.py_ver }}
161:       uv_ver: ${{ needs.load-vars.outputs.uv_ver }}
162:       ref: ${{ needs.authorize.outputs.test_ref }}
163: 
164:   report:
165:     needs:
166:       - create-check
167:       - build-containerlab
168:       - srsim-tests
169:     if: always() && needs.create-check.result == 'success'
170:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
171:     permissions:
172:       checks: write
173:     steps:
174:       - name: Update PR check
175:         uses: actions/github-script@v9
176:         env:
177:           CHECK_RUN_ID: ${{ needs.create-check.outputs.check_run_id }}
178:           BUILD_RESULT: ${{ needs.build-containerlab.result }}
179:           TEST_RESULT: ${{ needs.srsim-tests.result }}
180:         with:
181:           script: |
182:             const conclusions = {
183:               success: 'success',
184:               failure: 'failure',
185:               cancelled: 'cancelled',
186:               skipped: 'neutral',
187:             };
188:             const result =
189:               ['failure', 'cancelled'].includes(process.env.BUILD_RESULT)
190:                 ? process.env.BUILD_RESULT
191:                 : process.env.TEST_RESULT;
192:             const conclusion = conclusions[result] || 'failure';
193:             await github.rest.checks.update({
194:               owner: context.repo.owner,
195:               repo: context.repo.repo,
196:               check_run_id: Number(process.env.CHECK_RUN_ID),
197:               status: 'completed',
198:               conclusion,
199:               output: {
200:                 title: `srsim tests ${result}`,
201:                 summary: `The manual srsim test workflow finished with result: ${result}.`,
202:               },
203:             });

<path>/source/head/tests/rf-run.sh</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: #!/bin/bash
2: # Copyright 2020 Nokia
3: # Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
4: # SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
5: 
6: # arguments
7: # $1 - runtime: [docker, podman, c9s]
8: # $2 - test suite to execute
9: # $3... - optional arguments passed to robot
10: 
11: set -euo pipefail
12: 
13: if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
14:   echo "usage: $0 <runtime> <test suite>"
15:   exit 1
16: fi
17: 
18: runtime=$1
19: suite=$2
20: shift 2
21: extra_robot_args=("$@")
22: 
23: # set containerlab binary path to a value of CLAB_BIN env variable
24: # unless it is not set, then use 'containerlab' as a default value
25: if [ -z "${CLAB_BIN:-}" ]; then
26:   CLAB_BIN=containerlab
27: fi
28: 
29: export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
30: export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
31: 
32: echo "Running tests with containerlab binary at $(command -v "${CLAB_BIN}") path and selected runtime: ${runtime}"
33: 
34: COV_DIR=/tmp/clab-tests/coverage
35: 
36: # coverage output directory
37: mkdir -p "${COV_DIR}"
38: 
39: # parses the dir or file name passed to the rf-run.sh script
40: # and in case of a directory, it returns the name of the directory
41: # in case of a file it returns the name of the file's dir catenated with file name without extension
42: function get_logname() {
43:   path=$1
44:   filename=$(basename "$path")
45:   if [[ "$filename" == *.* ]]; then
46:     dirname=$(dirname "$path")
47:     basename=$(basename "$path" | cut -d. -f1)
48:     echo "${dirname##*/}-${basename}"
49:   else
50:     echo "${filename}"
51:   fi
52: }
53: 
54: robot_args=()
55: if [ "${runtime}" = "c9s" ]; then
56:   robot_args+=(--include clabernetes)
57: fi
58: 
59: GOCOVERDIR=${COV_DIR} uv run --project . -m robot \
60:   --consolecolors on \
61:   -r none \
62:   --variable CLAB_BIN:${CLAB_BIN} \
63:   --variable runtime:${runtime} \

        "text": "#!/bin/bash\n# Copyright 2020 Nokia\n# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.\n# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause\n\n# arguments\n# $1 - runtime: [docker, podman, c9s]\n# $2 - test suite to execute\n# $3... - optional arguments passed to robot\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nif [ \"$#\" -lt 2 ]; then\n  echo \"usage: $0 <runtime> <test suite>\"\n  exit 1\nfi\n\nruntime=$1\nsuite=$2\nshift 2\nextra_robot_args=(\"$@\")\n\n# set containerlab binary path to a value of CLAB_BIN env variable\n# unless it is not set, then use 'containerlab' as a default value\nif [ -z \"${CLAB_BIN:-}\" ]; then\n  CLAB_BIN=containerlab\nfi\n\nexport AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID\nexport AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY\n\necho \"Running tests with containerlab binary at $(command -v \"${CLAB_BIN}\") path and selected runtime: ${runtime}\"\n\nCOV_DIR=/tmp/clab-tests/coverage\n\n# coverage output directory\nmkdir -p \"${COV_DIR}\"\n\n# parses the dir or file name passed to the rf-run.sh script\n# and in case of a directory, it returns the name of the directory\n# in case of a file it returns the name of the file's dir catenated with file name without extension\nfunction get_logname() {\n  path=$1\n  filename=$(basename \"$path\")\n  if [[ \"$filename\" == *.* ]]; then\n    dirname=$(dirname \"$path\")\n    basename=$(basename \"$path\" | cut -d. -f1)\n    echo \"${dirname##*/}-${basename}\"\n  else\n    echo \"${filename}\"\n  fi\n}\n\nrobot_args=()\nif [ \"${runtime}\" = \"c9s\" ]; then\n  robot_args+=(--include clabernetes)\nfi\n\nGOCOVERDIR=${COV_DIR} uv run --project . -m robot \\\n  --consolecolors on \\\n  -r none \\\n  --variable CLAB_BIN:${CLAB_BIN} \\\n  --variable runtime:${runtime} \\\n  -l ./tests/out/$(get_logname \"${suite}\")-${runtime}-log \\\n  --output ./tests/out/$(basename \"${suite}\")-${runtime}-out.xml \\\n  \"${extra_robot_args[@]}\" \\\n  \"${robot_args[@]}\" \\\n  \"${suite}\"",

Reasoning
The docs don't show the exact TiMOS license boot-log lines. I can't verify the exact log format from the repo. The regexes are plausible.

Now, let me think about the fail-on-renewal logic more carefully. Reading again:

```
Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log
    ${valid} = status of: Should Match Regexp  excerpt  Loading TiMOS License ... OK
    ${expiration} = not found
    ${dates} = Get Regexp Matches excerpt 'The license installed on \S+ expires (.+)' 1
    ${expired} = status of: Should Match Regexp excerpt (?i)License has expired|expired license
    ${renewal} = no
    IF len($dates) > 0 → renewal=yes
    IF not ${valid} or ${expired} → renewal=yes
    print "License expiration: ${expiration}" / "License renewal required: ${renewal}"
    IF renewal==yes → Fail
```

Hmm — but wait. TiMOS prints "The license installed on <host> expires <date>" in the boot log ALWAYS at boot (I believe SR OS prints this informational line when the license loads successfully — e.g., "The license installed on sr13 expires 01/01/2027"). If it's always printed, this test would always fail... which contradicts a passing CI. If it's printed only near expiry (within e.g. 60 days?), then this check is a proactive renewal flag.

Actually, hmm. I recall SR OS prints at boot: "License expiration: 2026-11-04" style messages? Actually the console messages "License expiration: not found" and "License renewal required: yes" look machine-readable, meant for some external system to parse the CI log for license maintenance. Given no in-repo consumer, I cannot confirm intent. This could be intentional (the author wants to know when renewal needed, and intentionally fails the suite to signal). But failing a test because the license has an expiration date printed seems odd.

Hmm wait — re-read the docstring: "Expiration is printed only when the log contains it." That suggests the log normally does NOT contain expiration info (valid license), and only prints it when there's an issue (near expiry/expired). So the intended flow: if "The license installed on X expires Y" appears in the boot log → that indicates the license is nearing expiration → renewal required → fail (to alert maintainers). That's plausible and consistent.

OK, so I'll treat the fail-on-renewal as intended design (with a caveat maybe P4 note? It's speculative; skip or mention in coverage notes).

Now the real defect hunting:

**Bug candidate 1: `${expired}` check duplicates validity conditions but with `Run Keyword And Return Status` of Should Match Regexp on empty excerpt — fine.**

**Bug candidate 2: `Check SR-SIM License` sets Log Level NONE then INFO. If CI runs robot with DEBUG log level, this resets to INFO. Minor (P4-ish, probably not worth it).**

**Bug candidate 3: `Set Test Variable` vs suite-level callers — all callers are in test cases. Fine. BUT: what about `Deploy SR-SIM Lab` being used in `Suite Teardown` (Destroy only) — fine.**

Hmm wait, actually check 03-sros-dist-to-linux line 7: `Suite Teardown      Destroy SR-SIM Lab    ...` — destroy only. Fine.

**Bug candidate 4: The 45-second wait may be too short for the license line to appear?** The boot log license line is printed early during TiMOS boot; container logs stream from t=0. 45s × retries 5s ≈ up to 45s. SR-SIM boot to TiMOS start could take longer than 45s? The CPM container boots TiMOS; from lab experience, "Loading TiMOS License" appears within the first minute. Risky but plausible; can't verify. Not a finding unless evidence.

**Bug candidate 5: In `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt`, when no srsim containers exist (e.g., Check called after destroy or wrong lab), names empty → boot grep on `${topo dir}/clab-${lab}` which may not exist → excerpt empty → Boot Log Contains License Result fails after 45s → Clear failure. OK.

**Bug candidate 6: `String.Split To Lines` on trailing empty line → empty element → `${runtime} logs ''` runs `docker logs ''` → error message piped to grep → no match → empty part. Harmless noise in the excerpt? Actually `docker logs ''` outputs "Error: name can't be empty" (stderr), piped into grep (2>&1) → "Error: name can't be empty" not matching license patterns → contributes nothing. OK.

Hmm wait, actually: `String.Split To Lines` — RF String library keyword "Split To Lines" splits string into lines; for "a\nb\n" it returns ['a', 'b'] (I believe it strips the trailing newline; actually Split To Lines handles \n; trailing empty element? `Split To Lines("a\nb\n")` → ['a','b']? Let me recall implementation: `Split To Lines` uses `splitlines()`? Actually `String.Split To Lines(string, start=0, end=None)` — it splits by lines and returns all lines; implementation: `return string.splitlines()[start:end]`? I believe it's `lines = string.splitlines()` then slice. `"a\nb\n".splitlines()` → ['a','b']. No trailing empty. Good.

**Bug candidate 7: Docker `ps -aq` with `--format '{{.Names}}'`**: `-a` includes stopped containers; fine.

**Bug candidate 8: In 12-srsim-multi-mgmt, the lab is deployed with initial-vars in test 1; test 2 `Check SR-SIM license` runs Check. Then later tests manipulate. Note: `Apply moves the integrated node to another management network` — apply moves the integrated node to a different mgmt network and recreates it? The container might be recreated — the license check already ran. Fine.

**Bug candidate 9: In 11-srsim-apply, `Check SR-SIM License` is invoked in test 1 only — after the initial apply with `no-links-vars`. The lab `srsim-apply` has nodes R1 (standalone?) and R2 (distributed). OK.

**Bug candidate 10: The grep for bootlog uses `--include=bootlog.txt` with `-R` under `${topo dir}/clab-${lab}` — that's the lab dir. bootlog.txt exists per docs in each node dir (e.g., `nodes/R1/log/bootlog.txt`? The docs structure shows `├── log` with bootlog.txt?). Let me check the docs snippet around line 830-860 of sros.md to confirm path.

**Bug candidate 11: The `\S+` in `The license installed on \\S+ expires (.+)` — the actual log line is "The license installed on <HOSTNAME> expires <DATE>"? If the actual TiMOS line is "The license installed on ThisHost expires 2026-11-04" fine. Can't verify format.

Now — one more important check: does the "OK" ever appear with the pattern `from location:'...' ... OK`? The doc sros.md lines 840-880 might show a bootlog excerpt with the exact license lines. Let me read that section of docs to validate the regexes.

Note: `mgmt-tests.yml` runs `./tests/15-mgmt/12*.robot` with `${{ inputs.runtime }}` which for srsim is docker only? The mgmt suite Setup skips when runtime != docker. But it also runs under podman (continue-on-error). The suite skips when runtime != docker (Skip If in Suite Setup). Good.

Now, one thing about `12-srsim-multi-mgmt` under podman: it skips. Good.

But wait — there's an issue: in the mgmt suite, the `Check SR-SIM license` test case runs `Check SR-SIM License ${topo} ${runtime}` where `${topo}` is an absolute path — fine.

Now, an important scenario in the mgmt suite: after the check, the suite later applies `moved-vars` which RE-CREATES the integrated node on a different network, then destroys. Fine.

But here's a subtle issue with the multi-mgmt suite and the license-check: SR-SIM `sr-int` gets mgmt-ipv4/mgmt-ipv6; the container may have TWO nodes for the distributed node (a, 1). All labeled nokia_srsim. OK.

Now, the other significant issue to check: **`Check SR-SIM License` when the distributed node's CPM container hasn't printed license lines to stdout?** The container logs vs bootlog fallback covers both.

Now, let's think about **the 45s window in the apply test after `Apply`**: The apply command completes when nodes are started; TiMOS boot begins. The "Loading TiMOS License" line appears within seconds. OK.

Next, consider **the `IF not ${valid} or ${expired}`** — RF `IF` with `not ${valid} or ${expired}` — evaluates as Python expression: `not False or False` → True. OK.

**Now, `${dates}` — `Get Regexp Matches` returns list; if the pattern doesn't match (valid license, no expiration notice), renewal=no, valid=True → pass.** OK.

But here's the catch: The expiration line "The license installed on \S+ expires (.+)" — is it printed in EVERY boot? If TiMOS prints it every boot (I actually believe SR OS does print "The license installed on ... expires ..." at every boot! Let me think... In SR OS, at boot with a valid license, the boot log contains:

```
Loading TiMOS License for 'SR-1-24D' from location:'cf3:/license.txt' ... OK
```

and I do NOT recall an always-printed expiration line. There IS a TiMOS behavior where when the license is about to expire (within ~30/60 days), it prints warnings like "The license installed on this node expires on <date>". I believe the expiration notice is printed only near expiry — the docstring says "Expiration is printed only when the log contains it", which strongly suggests conditional. Given the docstring, the author believes the same. OK — treat as intended.

So finding stands: with docker, `ps -aq --format '{{.Names}}'` returns IDs, not names. The subsequent `docker logs '<id>'` works, so tests pass; but the format string is dead/misleading, and with podman the combination may behave differently (podman respects --format when given, ignoring -q — which would give names; also fine for logs). Reasoning
Now let me nail down the key findings. Let me carefully evaluate the most significant potential defects.

**Finding A: `Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log` reads `${license_excerpt}` — a test-scope variable set by `Boot Log Contains License Result` via `Set Test Variable`.**

Scope check: All callers of `Check SR-SIM License` are inside test cases (verify: Deploy SR-SIM Lab is called from test cases in 13-srsim suites; in 15-mgmt/12, the check is in a test case). So `Set Test Variable` works. But is there any suite where `Deploy SR-SIM Lab` is called from Suite Setup? Earlier I verified none. OK.

However — there IS a subtle RF subtlety: `Set Test Variable` sets a test-scope variable. `Check SR-SIM License` is called directly within the test → variable visible to `Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log` in the same test. Fine. Not a finding.

**Finding B: `docker ps -aq --format '{{.Names}}'` returns container IDs, not names.**

Evidence: docker CLI's `-q/--quiet` takes precedence over `--format` (the formatter emits only IDs). The intent of `--format '{{.Names}}'` is defeated; it works only because `docker logs` accepts IDs as well. Under podman, `--format` and `-q` combined: podman ps docs state `-q` prints numeric IDs only and `--format` takes precedence over `-q`? Actually I recall podman: "If --format is specified, it takes precedence over --quiet". Hmm — actually I'm not sure podman combines them gracefully. Since both suites that exercise this keyword run under docker (`${runtime} docker`, and the 15-mgmt suite skips on non-docker), the impact is minimal today. Also — `--filter label=clab-node-kind=nokia_srsim` — do component containers carry this label? Let me check nodes/sros component creation. In 12-srsim-multi-mgmt, distributed node `sr-dist` creates `clab-sr13-sr-dist-a` and `clab-sr13-sr-dist-1` containers — do those get the `clab-node-kind` label? Labels are set generically in nodes container creation via `nodes/node.go` createContainer labels: `clab-node-kind: n.Kind()`. Component containers are created via the sros component logic — do they use the generic label set? Let me check nodes/sros/ component creation to confirm. This matters: if component containers lack the label, the `ps` filter misses them, and their logs wouldn't be examined — but the bootlog grep covers cf3 anyway. Let me check.

**Finding C: duplication** — the grep alternation string and the Loading regex are each defined twice (lines 66/70 and 50/80). P4 maintainability.

**Finding D: `Set Log Level INFO` hardcoded restore** — if CI ran robot with TRACE/DEBUG, the level is downgraded to INFO. rf-run.sh doesn't set a level. Minor; probably fold into finding C? It's a separate micro-issue; I'd likely skip or make P4. Hmm — the "Set Log Level NONE / INFO" pattern: the purpose is to keep the log clean during retries. Restoring INFO is correct in this repo's default. Not worth a finding; skip.

**Finding E: The `Fail` message when no license result lacks the excerpt** — P4 diagnostic improvement. Could mention.

**Finding F: 45-second wait budget** — plausible; coverage note.

**Finding G: renewal=yes when any expiration date is found** — intended per docstring; coverage note.

Let me now check the component container label question and also whether `clab-node-kind` label is applied to all containers created by clab (generic). Check nodes/node.go for label assignment and nodes/sros for component containers.

## PR Review: SR-SIM license check in robot tests

### Summary

This revision adds an SR-SIM license verification mechanism to the Robot Framework suite. `tests/srsim.robot` gains three keywords (`Check SR-SIM License`, `Boot Log Contains License Result`, `Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log`, plus helper `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt`), `Deploy SR-SIM Lab` now invokes the check after every deploy, and two suites (`11-srsim-apply.robot`, `12-srsim-multi-mgmt.robot`) invoke it directly. I traced all callers, the label plumbing for component containers, the boot-log file provenance, and the CI workflows:

- All callers of `Deploy SR-SIM Lab`/`Check SR-SIM License` run inside test cases (none in Suite Setup), so the `Set Test Variable` handoff of `${license_excerpt}` is scope-safe.
- Component and netns-holder containers inherit `clab-node-kind=nokia_srsim` because `nodes/sros/sros.go` deep-copies `n.Cfg`, whose labels are populated by `core/config.go` (`cfg.Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] = cfg.Kind`), so the `ps` filter in the new helper matches CPM/component containers too.
- `bootlog.txt` lives under `${lab dir}/<node>/config/cf3/`, so the `grep -R --include=bootlog.txt` fallback is correctly rooted.
- Both exercising suites are Docker-only: the `13-srsim` shard in `srsim-tests.yml` runs with the default `runtime: docker`, and `12-srsim-multi-mgmt.robot` skips itself on non-Docker runtimes.
- The `15-mgmt` suite gates itself on license presence via Suite Setup, so no-license environments skip safely; `srsim-tests.yml` only runs when the `SRSIM_LICENSE` secret exists.

The overall approach is sound. I found one diagnosability defect and two maintainability issues in the new keyword file; the two suite edits are correct.

### Findings

| Priority | Count | Summary |
|----------|-------|---------|
| P3 | 1 | Failed license check suppresses all diagnostic evidence |
| P4 | 2 | Dead `--format` under `docker ps -aq`; duplicated regex/grep patterns |

#### P3 — Failed license check discards all diagnostic evidence and synthesizes a report it never measured- **Location:** [tests/srsim.robot#L30-L41](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L30-L41)
- **Problem:** `Check SR-SIM License` sets the log level to `NONE` for the whole 45-second retry window (`Wait Until Keyword Succeeds 45 seconds 5 seconds`). Because `Run` logs its stdout at INFO level, every command (`${runtime} ps -aq ...`, `${runtime} logs '<id>' | grep ...`, the boot-log `grep -R`) and every collected excerpt is suppressed from the test log. If the retry fails, the test is failed with only the static message `SR-SIM boot log has no license result`, and the not-found branch additionally prints fabricated report values (`License renewal required: yes`) for a measurement that never happened.
- **Trigger:** Any failed license check — a slow CI runner where the license line is not flushed within 45 seconds, a TiMOS log format drift, or an unreachable runtime — produces a test failure with zero evidence in the log, both locally and in the `srsim-tests.yml` CI artifacts.
- **Impact:** Maintainers cannot distinguish "license line not yet flushed" from "pattern no longer matches" or "runtime inaccessible" without re-running the suite manually. This directly undermines the purpose of the check, which is to make license problems diagnosable.
- **Correction:** In the failure branch, restore the log level (or use a level that passes the filter), call `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt` once more, and `Log` the excerpt (plus the resolved container names) before `Fail`. Also avoid asserting `License renewal required: yes` when nothing was measured; `License expiration: not found` alone is honest.

#### P4 — `docker ps -aq` with `--format '{{.Names}}'` returns container IDs, not names
- **Location:** [tests/srsim.robot#L60-L62](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L60-L62)
- **Problem:** In Docker CLI, `-q`/`--quiet` takes precedence over `--format`, so `${names}` contains container IDs, not the names the template requests. The keyword only works because `docker logs` also accepts IDs. Podman resolves the `--format`/`-q` conflict differently, so the two runtimes silently produce different values from the same command.
- **Trigger:** Every execution of `SR-SIM License Log Excerpt` under Docker (which is the only runtime that reaches these suites today).
- **Impact:** No functional failure today, but the format string is dead code that misleads readers into thinking names are collected, and it creates a latent divergence if a future Podman-enabled suite reuses the keyword. Note the rest of the repo gets this right — e.g., `09-srsim-pause-container.robot` uses `docker ps -a --filter ... --format '{{.Names}}'` without `-q`.
- **Correction:** Drop `-q` and keep `--format '{{.Names}}'` (matching the pattern used elsewhere in the test suite), or drop `--format` and accept IDs explicitly.

#### P4 — License regex and grep patterns are duplicated across three keywords
- **Location:** [tests/srsim.robot#L48-L51](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L48-L51), [#L66](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L66), [#L70](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L70), [#L78-L85](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/22903a3e44fc00eb5d2d392cc8e702725460e643/tests/srsim.robot#L78-L85)
- **Problem:** The TiMOS license-load regex appears verbatim in both `Boot Log Contains License Result` (line 50) and `Report SR-SIM License From Boot Log` (line 80), and the four-alternative grep pattern appears verbatim in both the per-container command (line 66) and the boot-log command (line 70). The paired `Log To Console` + `Log` calls (four lines for two messages, repeated twice) and the second `Set Log Level NONE`/`INFO` pair in `Report` extend the same duplication.
- **Trigger:** Any future adjustment — e.g., when TiMOS changes the license-load wording — must be applied in multiple places; missing one makes the waiting keyword succeed while the report keyword silently misclassifies the license.
- **Impact:** Divergence risk in exactly the logic this PR is meant to centralize.
- **Correction:** Define the license regex and grep pattern once as suite-level variables in the `*** Variables ***` section of `tests/srsim.robot` (or collapse the two `Report` keywords' duplicated reporting lines into one), and reuse them from all call sites.

### Coverage notes

- This was a source-only review; no tests were executed and no TiMOS log output was observed, so the exact boot-log line formats (`Loading TiMOS License for ... from location:'...' ... OK`, `The license installed on ... expires ...`, `License has expired`) and the timing of the license-load line could not be verified against real output. The patterns are plausible but unverifiable from the repository.
- The `45 seconds` total budget in `Check SR-SIM License` is an intentional choice I cannot validate; if TiMOS prints the license line later on slow runners, this becomes a flaky failure mode across all eight suites that use `Deploy SR-SIM Lab`. Not reported as a finding for lack of evidence.
- The report treats *any* captured expiration date as `renewal required` (`len($dates) > 0`). Per the keyword documentation ("Expiration is printed only when the log contains it"), this appears to be an intentional near-expiry signal; if TiMOS were ever to print an expiration line on every boot, all license-gated suites would fail. Left as a noted risk rather than a defect.
- Stale `bootlog.txt` files from a previous, un-cleaned lab run could theoretically satisfy the check with old content; `Destroy SR-SIM Lab` uses `--cleanup` and every exercising suite tears down, so the exposure is limited and not reported as a finding.
- Verified the `clab-node-kind=nokia_srsim` label reaches component and netns-holder containers, all referenced topologies declare `kind: nokia_srsim`, and `Should Match Regexp` search semantics (multiline, unanchored) are consistent with pre-existing patterns in `11-srsim-apply.robot`.
- No documentation or schema impact: the change is confined to test code with no user-visible CLI/topology behavior.
